segments.text: Welcome to the Daily Robotics Brief, August 16th, 2026.
I'm your host, and we've got the latest updates on the robotics industry.
Humanoid robots are in the spotlight with regulation in San Mateo County, a promising return on investment for Figure's CEO, and LG's upcoming innovation in humanoids powered by NVIDIA Isaac GR00T.
From Humanoids Daily, "San Mateo County Moves to Regulate Humanoid Robots, Threatening Teleoperation Business Models."

San Mateo County has taken a significant step towards regulating humanoid robots, with the unanimous passage of a resolution that will mandate the creation of a comprehensive permitting process for commercial humanoid robots.
The proposed ordinance will require humanoid robots to be supervised at all times by a trained, on-site human, as well as undergo economic impact assessments to mitigate potential job displacement.

The county will also impose annual cost-recovery fees, which will fund specialized HazMat equipment for local first responders and strict hardware vetting to ensure a clean manufacturer safety record.

This move is expected to have a substantial impact on the teleoperation business models that rely heavily on humanoid robots, as they will now be required to ensure the presence of human supervision and safety protocols.
From Humanoids Daily, "Figure CEO Brett Adcock Claims Humanoids Are Already Delivering ROI Amid Severe Labor Shortages."
According to Figure AI's CEO, Brett Adcock, the primary challenge in the humanoid sector is not in manufacturing hardware, but in achieving high-level onboard AI.
Early commercial partners have achieved a return on investment, with severe labor shortages and annual turnover rates exceeding 100% in some sectors.
This shift in focus has enabled Figure to concentrate on solving critical labor shortages for enterprise clients.
As a result, the company is now leveraging the benefits of its humanoid technology to drive ROI for its clients.
From Humanoids Daily, "LG to Unveil Next-Gen Humanoid Built on NVIDIA Isaac GR00T in Early 2027."
LG is developing a next-generation humanoid robot powered by NVIDIA's Isaac GR00T foundation model and Jetson Thor compute platform, set to be unveiled in Q1 2027.
The robot will utilize LG's internal supply chain resources, leveraging actuators, sensors, and batteries developed in-house.
LG plans to gather real-world training data by deploying its CLOiD wheel-based robots at its Tennessee washing machine manufacturing plant.
Additionally, the company will build an 80 MW AI factory in Cheonan, South Korea, by 2028 to process physical AI datasets.
This project marks a significant milestone in the integration of AI and robotics, demonstrating LG's commitment to advancing humanoid robotics technology.
"What a day in the world of robotics - San Mateo's got its eye on the future, and it's not just a 'bot!
Thanks for joining me on this robotic roundup, I'll see you tomorrow when the machines will surely be back online.
Until then, keep on charging!"
